title: The Mizo insurgency, 1961-1987 (detailed)

subtitles.text: *October 1961.* After the Mautam famine, Laldenga's famine front becomes the *Mizo National Front*
*1963.* Laldenga crosses into *East Pakistan*: arms and training camps follow
*28 February 1966*, night: the MNF attacks *1 Assam Rifles* at Aizawl, Lunglei and Champhai
BSF posts are hit too: *Chawngte, Demagiri, Hnahlan, Marpara, Tipaimukh, Tuipang, Vaphai*
*1 March.* The MNF declares *independence*
*2 March.* Assam declares the whole Mizo district *disturbed* under the Armed Forces Special Powers Act
*3 March.* The 8th Sikh battalion starts down the road from *Silchar*
That night an Assam Rifles patrol is *ambushed* at Chanmari, Aizawl: *5 jawans* are killed
*5 March*, 10 a.m.: Toofani and Hunter jets appear over *Aizawl*
*6 March.* Heavier bombing: houses in *Dawrpui* and *Chhinga Veng* burn; residents flee to the hills
*7 March.* The army reaches Aizawl; the MNF falls back toward *Lunglei*
*8 March.* 2/11 *Gorkha Rifles* head for Champhai, 3 *Bihar* for Lunglei
*14 March.* Lunglei is secured
*15 March.* Champhai is secured; all four battalions of *61 Mountain Brigade* are in the hills
By *25 March* every town is retaken; MNF leaders take refuge in *East Pakistan*
*January 1967.* Village pickets fail, and villagers are moved into guarded *Protected and Progressive Villages*
*31 January 1967.* Air Force jets strike *Hmuntlang* village; Delhi denies it
MNA fighters *ambush* convoys near *Saiha, Tuipang* and *Demagiri*, then slip over the border
The first grouping moves *106 villages* into *18 centres*: 52,210 people
*August 1968.* Under an amnesty, *1,524* MNF members surrender
*5 November 1968.* Assam Rifles raid an MNF camp; *3 riflemen* are killed
*1969.* A second phase moves *184 villages* into *40 centres*: 97,339 people
*1971.* Mizo fighters operate with the Pakistan Army in the *Chittagong Hill Tracts*
*December 1971.* Indian forces enter the Hill Tracts and overrun the *MNF camps*
The MNF flees into *Burma*. On *21 January 1972*, Mizoram becomes a Union Territory
*1974.* From London, Laldenga sends his terms to *Indira Gandhi*
*13 January 1975.* MNA gunmen in police uniform kill three senior officers at Aizawl *police HQ*
*1976.* A partial accord with Laldenga (sources differ: February or July)
*4 April 1980.* Laldenga meets Indira Gandhi and orders an MNF *ceasefire*
*1982.* Talks collapse and the MNF is *banned* again
*October 1984.* New talks stall when Indira Gandhi is *assassinated*
*15 February 1985.* Laldenga meets *Rajiv Gandhi*; talks resume
*30 June 1986.* Laldenga and Home Secretary R. D. Pradhan sign the *Mizoram Accord*
Arms are handed over, and on *21 August 1986* Laldenga heads a new government
*20 February 1987.* Mizoram becomes a *state* of India
